# @roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth

English | [中文](./docs/README.zh.md)

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) provider
plugin for a Loomy (iFlytek) account. You sign in with Loomy's phone-code
sign-in, your chats go through Loomy's OpenAI-compatible model gateway, and
your points — the permanent balance and the daily grant, two wallets — and the
daily first-login refresh that renews the grant land on the Usage card.

| Provider id | Sign-in | Upstream hosts |
|---|---|---|
| `loomy` | phone code (+86) | `loomyad.xunfei.cn` (account plane `account.xfinfr.com`) |

The package exports `LoomyAuthPlugin` (`loomy`) for magpie and OpenCode
v1, and — from 0.2.0 — a default export (`{ id: "loomy-auth", setup,
server }`) for OpenCode ≥ 2.x, with the `server` function the same V1
factory for hosts that read object entrypoints (magpie's own loader
among them). One package, every host.

## Install

```sh
magpie plugin add github:road-kid/opencode-loomy-auth    # this repository
magpie plugin add @roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth  # the npm name
magpie plugin add .                                      # a local copy — no npm, no GitHub
magpie plugin login loomy      # the phone-code sign-in
magpie provider test loomy     # one small request per API, to check the wiring
magpie quota                   # the points card
```

The same package loads in OpenCode (the `"plugin"` array in `opencode.json`,
then `opencode auth login`) — for OpenCode ≥ 2.x, see
[OpenCode v2](#opencode-v2). magpie keeps the sign-in in `plugin-auth.json`
(mode 600); OpenCode keeps it in `auth.json`.

## OpenCode v2

From 0.2.0 the package loads in OpenCode ≥ 2.x as a default-export plugin
(`{ id: "loomy-auth", setup }`), beside the named export magpie and
OpenCode v1 read. Same code, same sign-in, same gateway.

### Install

Three ways, pick one:

- the `plugins` key of `opencode.json(c)` with the npm name:
  `"plugins": ["@roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth"]`;
- the same key with a local directory:
  `"plugins": ["E:/path/to/opencode-loomy-auth"]` — the path must be a
  directory, a file path is skipped;
- or the directory itself into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (global) or
  `.opencode/plugins/` (project) — OpenCode discovers it on its own and
  hot-reloads it when files change.

### Sign-in

`opencode auth login` (or `/connect` in the TUI) → pick the Loomy
integration → the phone-code way → the 11-digit phone number → the SMS
arrives (six digits, five minutes to live) → type the code → done. The
session lasts fourteen days and there is no refresh — when it ends, sign
in again. The desktop OpenCode's account-connection screen reads the same
server APIs.

### Models

Signed in, the `loomy` provider appears on its own; before that it is
hidden — the hiding is the design, a dead model is what it prevents. The
model list is read live from the gateway's `/api/v1/models` and refreshes
as the sign-in state changes; when the gateway is unreachable the plugin
falls back to the built-in 2026-11-17 snapshot (chat models only). Bearer
auth on the gateway calls is injected by the host itself. The rows carry
the vendors' own display names — a model the name table doesn't know
keeps its cleaned gateway name with the leading brand word set right —
and the reasoning gears its vendor's docs name — a curated per-model table
(DeepSeek and GLM: low / high / max, the DeepSeek menu also read off the
desktop picker; qwen: low / medium / xhigh; MiMo: no gears at all (its
docs run thinking on a thinking.type switch); Spark:
none / low / high), not the gateway's five-level `reasoning_efforts` stamp,
which is boilerplate and wrong for all six. A row the table does not name
keeps its declaration passed through as it stands; a row that declares
nothing — `auto` — falls back to the fixed low/medium/high. The picker's
Default sends no field and the gateway's own default gear applies.

### Points in the TUI, and the daily renewal

Type `/loomy` (or find "Loomy 积分面板" in the command palette) for a small
panel: the sign-in state, the points total, and the daily grant with its
remaining over its size and its reset moment in Beijing time — with
**check in now** (the same first-login call the Check in now button makes,
worded the same way) and **refresh** beside them. The day's renewal also
runs by itself: at load, behind every credential event and on a half-hour
timer, the same once-a-day claim goes out silently — a success is marked
per Beijing day, a failure just waits for the next event or tick to ask
again. The desktop OpenCode carries the same panel in its own windows —
entry is the desktop's side-panel launcher, through the package's
`./gui-experimental` bundle — and that export name is the upstream's own
admission: the GUI plugin API is experimental and may change between
desktop releases.

### What stays magpie-only

The Usage card, the check-in switch and the image-generator roster ride
magpie's own host-extension hooks — those stay magpie-only, while the
`/loomy` panel above brings the points' numbers to the v2 TUI itself.
There the plugin is the phone-code sign-in, the live model list, the
gateway chat, and the panel.

## Signing in

The sign-in is Loomy's phone-code one, in two steps:

- magpie asks for the phone number first (mainland China, 11 digits; a leading
  `+86` or `86`, spaces and hyphens are cleaned off before the check);
- the plugin sends the SMS code (it lives five minutes), magpie opens a
  six-digit code box, and the plugin trades the code for the session.

The session lasts fourteen days and Loomy offers no refresh. When it ends
(HTTP 401/403, or the business codes `020002`/`100002`), the plugin marks
the sign-in expired and magpie asks for a new SMS sign-in — there is nothing
to renew. The account's id is the masked phone (`138****8000`); the Loomy userid
is kept with the credential.

The account host checks an HMAC-SHA1 signature on both sign-in calls.
The signature belongs to the account plane alone — the gateway
planes never sign.

## Requests

Chats are OpenAI Chat (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) sent to
`https://loomyad.xunfei.cn/api/v1/chat/completions`, the request body passed
through untouched. The session token rides in both headers the gateway reads —
`token:` and `Authorization: Bearer`, the client's own dual write.

A refusal whose words say the points or quota ran out (a 402, 403 or 429 that
says so) goes on as a 429 `rate_limit_error`, so magpie can move the
conversation to another account. Any other 401/403 is the sign-in's end.

## Models

Signed in, the model list is read live from `GET /api/v1/models`: capabilities
become the tool / reasoning / image bits, the context and output limits pass
through, and every model carries the reasoning gears its vendor's docs name
(the curated per-model table: DeepSeek and GLM low / high / max, qwen
low / medium / xhigh, MiMo no gears, Spark none / low / high), a row
the table does not name falling back to its `reasoning_efforts` declaration
as it stands — with the fixed low/medium/high only for a row that declares
none. The
gateway prints each model's point rate as a suffix on its display name
(`MiniMax M3 （x4.0）` — ASCII and full-width brackets both
occur); the plugin splits that off — the name stays clean, and the rate
rides the model record, the field the host's picker reads the multiplier
from. A model the
upstream itself declares free — the words 免费 in the name, or a rate of
exactly zero — carries a `free` bit; no rate at all is not free. Rows that
aren't chat models stay off the chat list — the image generators say so in
their `type`, and carry an image generator's name besides, read by the same
words the host's own image-model catalog reads, so a row that ships no
`type` at all stays off just the same: chatting into one is a failure.

The image generators come back beside the chat list from a roster the
plugin itself keeps — the three it vouches for, each under the display
name the roster gives it, with the live row's own facts (the limits, the
capability bits) riding beside and the record's `api.url` aimed at the
gateway's own image route — `{apiBase}/images/generations` — not the chat
one. An entry is in the table only while the
live catalog names its id: a generator Loomy retires leaves at the next
answer with no release needed, and a generator it adds waits for the
release that names it here. No entry is in the fallback tables — with no
live answer there is no proof a generator still exists, and a dead draw
entry is what the roster exists to prevent. On the host side a listed
generator lands in the provider's Image models row when its id is one the
host's own image-model catalog reads (`qwen-image`, `seedream`… —
`Hy-Image` is not among those words), and until the host learns to keep a
plugin's generators out of the chat list too (yetone/magpie#2792) they
show there as chips as well: leave them unticked, and no agent chats into
one.

The live list is the source of truth and wins the moment it answers. Without
a session, on an empty answer or a failed ask, the plugin falls back to the
built-in table in the code — a snapshot of this same catalog's text models
as measured on 2026-11-17, aging only as the gateway's own catalog moves
on; the snapshot's rates and free bits go back to the host with it, and a
failed ask is marked as one, so the editor knows the list is the plugin's
defaults and not the account's. The table below is what the gateway itself
served on that day, kept here as a field guide:

| Model | Display name | Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spark-x2.6` | Spark-X2.6 正式版(限时免费) | x0.0 | thinking |
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | x2.0 | thinking, image |
| `deepseek-v4-flash-1017` | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 | x2.0 | thinking, image |
| `GLM-5.3-Flash` | GLM 5.3 Flash | x0.8 | thinking, image |
| `qwen3.8-flash` | qwen 3.8 flash | x0.8 | thinking, image |
| `mimo-v2.5` | MiMo V2.5 | x3.3 | thinking, image, audio |
| `auto` | 自动 · 均衡 | — | the gateway's own router |
| `Hy-Image-3.5-preview` | Hy image 3.5 preview | — | image generation |
| `doubao-seedream-5-lite` | Doubao seedream 5 lite | — | image generation |
| `qwen-image-3.0-pro` | qwen image 3.0 pro | — | image generation |

The three image-generation rows declare `output_modalities: ["image"]` —
they draw pictures rather than answer in text, and that is why they take
the image route: measured 2026-11-17, the chat route answers each of them
with 404 ("this model is not open yet"), while `images/generations` with
`{model, prompt, n}` draws. Their records hang no reasoning-effort
variants — a generator has no gears to offer. What a model's editor chip
says beside an older build's list: a generator ticked then and unticked
now is the roster's entry back again, no longer a pick the list has
forgotten.

## Usage

The usage card shows the two wallets Loomy keeps:

- the balance line: permanent + daily grant, added together (the answer's
  own total when it names one);
- a daily-grant window: the grant's consumed share as its percentage, with
  what is left over the limit beside it. `dailyBalance` is the grant's
  *remaining* (`dailyQuota` − `dailyConsumed`), so the percentage needs the
  grant's size: the pair the answer carries when it carries one, else the
  `dailyQuota` the check-in notes per account — the note lives on the
  credential itself (the host's own store, carried across plugin upgrades;
  a small file beside the plugin stands in where the host has no such
  store). A card that finds no note anywhere asks the first-login answer
  itself — once, the call being idempotent for the day (the client makes it
  on every login) — so a fresh install heals on its first render instead of
  waiting for the next check-in; no share is invented and no quota is
  assumed. The wording follows the interface language the host keeps in
  its settings (Chinese, or English beside it). The window carries the cycle's exact reset
  moment — the next Beijing midnight of the day the check-in's answer named
  — so the card counts down to the real refill, not a guessed one;
- the permanent row set aside: the permanent balance, which has no window;
- the newcomer row beside them: the one-time newcomer tasks (10000 points
  in all) while any stand unclaimed — an aside, never a percentage: a
  purse spent once has no window to consume. The check-in claims them;
  until it runs, the row says what is still claimable.

Loomy has no dedicated balance or check-in endpoint: the summary rides on the
points-records call, and the "check-in" is the first-login call the Loomy
client itself makes on every login. The server renews the daily grant once a
day, and the answer's `alreadyProcessed` tells the day's renewal from a
repeat: a repeat reports *done* ("今日已刷新", with what is left of the grant),
and the day's first reports *claimed* — with the gain as its credit when the
answer carries the whole arithmetic (`dailyQuota` − `dailyConsumed`), and the
remaining in the message otherwise.

## Check-in

The automatic daily run is magpie's, not the plugin's: the **Daily check-in**
switch lives in Settings → Usage → Plugins, ships with **magpie ≥ v0.1.1083**
and is **off by default** — turn it on and magpie runs the refresh once a day
per account (only a failed outcome retries that day). The **Check in now**
button runs it then and there. OpenCode doesn't call this hook.

The same run also claims the one-time newcomer tasks (the eight worth 10000
points in all): serially, highest value first, idempotent — and a refusal
among them never touches the daily claim's own result. The first check-in of
a fresh account typically refreshes the grant and lands the newcomer purse
in one go.

## Known limits

- **The session is fourteen days, with no refresh.** When it ends the only way
  on is a new SMS sign-in.
- **The point rate exists only as the display name's suffix.** Loomy ships no
  structured rate field; the plugin splits the suffix off but cannot verify
  any amount against the catalog.
- **Image input differs per model family.** The gateway's live rows
  declare image input for the vision families (read 2026-11-17: the
  DeepSeek pair, GLM, qwen, MiMo), and the plugin's records carry the
  bit in every spelling a host reads — flat, nested, and the
  `capabilities.input` mapping magpie's image badge marks off — so the
  badge shows. The wire shape is another matter, verified on the earlier
  catalog's `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` (since retired): it read only the
  gateway's private `<image_base64>…</image_base64>` marker (a standard
  `image_url` is cut off as text), while the GLM models are the
  opposite — only `image_url`, and the marker breaks them. Translating
  to each family's shape is a planned second iteration; until it lands,
  a host's own attachment flow is reliable on the GLM family alone, and
  the current DeepSeek rows' shape on this gateway is unverified.
- **`reasoning_effort` is ignored on non-thinking models.** The variants
  follow the curated per-vendor level table (DeepSeek and GLM low / high /
  max, qwen low / medium / xhigh, MiMo no gears, Spark none / low /
  high); a row the table does not name keeps its `reasoning_efforts`
  declaration as it stands, with the fixed low/medium/high only as the
  fallback for a row that declares none. The upstream drops the field on
  the models that don't think — a known behavior. Which models think is
  whatever the live catalog declares — on 2026-11-17 most text models did,
  not only the spark pair.
- **Streaming tool calls are not yet verified on a real account.** The
  desktop gateway's tool_calls streaming has no recorded real-machine run
  behind it; it is the first thing to check with your agent's tool loop. If
  it fails, the toolcall bit gets turned down in a future release.
- **The newcomer tasks are claimed by the check-in.** The eight one-off
  tasks (10000 points in all) are queried and claimed on every check-in —
  serially, highest value first, and idempotent: a repeat answers
  `alreadyCompleted` and pays nothing twice. A refusal among them never
  touches the daily claim's own result, and their still-claimable sum shows
  on the card as an aside row while any stands. The upstream judges
  completion its own way; the keys and values are the client's own task
  registry's.

## Disclaimer

This is an unofficial community package. It has nothing to do with iFlytek or
Loomy. The implementation is reverse-engineered from the desktop client's own
behavior and measured against it, for personal study and research. Your
phone number, your code and your session go only to Loomy's own hosts. The
points are for Loomy's own services; Loomy's terms decide where else they
may be used, and iFlytek hasn't approved that. The risk to the account is
yours. An upstream protocol change can break the package at any time.

## Development

```sh
node --test                       # the unit tests (node:test, a local fake upstream, no network)
node scripts/check.node.mjs      # the shape check, the same logic the community CI runs
```

The plugin itself is one `index.mjs` with no runtime dependencies — only
`node:crypto` and the standard `fetch` — and loads in Bun and Node ≥ 20.11
alike.

# @roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth

[English](../README.md) | 中文

一个面向 Loomy（讯飞）账号的 [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) / [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai)
provider 插件。用 Loomy 的手机验证码登录，对话经 Loomy 的 OpenAI 兼容模型网关转发，
积分——永久余额与每日赠送两个钱包——以及续满每日赠送的每日 first-login 刷新
都会落到用量卡上。

| Provider id | 登录方式 | 上游主机 |
|---|---|---|
| `loomy` | 手机验证码（+86） | `loomyad.xunfei.cn`（账号平面 `account.xfinfr.com`） |

本包导出 `LoomyAuthPlugin`（`loomy`）供 magpie 与 OpenCode v1 读取；从 0.2.0
起另有面向 OpenCode ≥ 2.x 的默认导出（`{ id: "loomy-auth", setup, server }`）
——其中 `server` 就是同一个 V1 工厂，供读取对象式入口的宿主调用（magpie
自己的加载器即属此类）。一个包，各种宿主。

## 安装

```sh
magpie plugin add github:road-kid/opencode-loomy-auth    # 本仓库
magpie plugin add @roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth  # npm 包名
magpie plugin add .                                      # 本地目录——不经 npm、不经 GitHub
magpie plugin login loomy      # 手机验证码登录
magpie provider test loomy     # 每个 API 发一条小请求，检查链路
magpie quota                   # 积分卡片
```

同一个包也能在 OpenCode 里加载（`opencode.json` 的 `"plugin"` 数组，
然后 `opencode auth login`）；OpenCode ≥ 2.x 走另一条安装路径——见下文
[OpenCode v2](#opencode-v2)。magpie 把登录态存在 `plugin-auth.json`
（mode 600）；OpenCode 存在 `auth.json`。

## OpenCode v2

从 0.2.0 起，本包以默认导出插件（`{ id: "loomy-auth", setup, server }`）的
形态在 OpenCode ≥ 2.x 中加载，与 magpie 和 OpenCode v1 读取的命名导出并存
（magpie 新版加载器读的 `server` 也在同一个默认导出里）。
同一份代码，同一种登录，同一个网关。

### 安装

三种方式，任选其一：

- `opencode.json(c)` 的 `plugins` 键填 npm 包名：
  `"plugins": ["@roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth"]`；
- 同一个键填本地目录：`"plugins": ["E:/path/to/opencode-loomy-auth"]`——
  路径必须是目录，文件路径会被跳过；
- 或把目录直接放进 `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`（全局）或
  `.opencode/plugins/`（项目级）——OpenCode 会自行发现，文件改动热重载。

### 登录

`opencode auth login`（或 TUI 里的 `/connect`）→ 选择 Loomy 集成 →
手机验证码方式 → 输入 11 位手机号 → 收到短信（6 位验证码，5 分钟有效）→
输入验证码 → 完成。会话有效期十四天，没有续期——到期重新登录即可。
桌面版 OpenCode 的账号连接界面用的是同一套服务端 API。

### 模型

登录后 `loomy` provider 自动出现；在那之前它不显示——隐藏正是设计，
防的就是死模型。模型清单实时读取自网关的 `/api/v1/models`，登录状态
变化时自动刷新；网关不可达时回落到内置的 2026-11-17 快照（仅聊天
模型）。网关调用上的 Bearer 认证由宿主自动注入。模型行用各厂商官方
拼写的展示名（名字表不认识的模型保留清洗后的网关名，仅把开头的
品牌词纠正为官方拼写），reasoning 档位按厂商文档策展的逐模型表：网关给
每行盖的通用五档 `reasoning_efforts` 戳（2026-11-17 六个在售思考模型都
声明 none/low/medium/high/xhigh）对六款模型全是错的——DeepSeek 与 GLM
为 low/high/max（DeepSeek 另有桌面选择器实测佐证），qwen 为
low/medium/xhigh，MiMo 无任何挡位（官方以 thinking.type 开关控制思考），
Spark 为 none/low/high。表内没有的
行仍按各行声明原样透传。不声明的行——`auto`——兜底 low/medium/high 三档。
picker 的 Default 不发字段，落到网关自己的默认档。

### 积分面板与每日续满

输入 `/loomy`（或在命令面板找「Loomy 积分面板」）唤出一个小面板：登录
状态、积分总额、每日赠送的剩余/总量与北京时间重置时刻，旁边两个动作——
**立即签到**（与「立即签到」按钮同一个 first-login 调用、同一套结果
文案）与**刷新**。每日续满也会在后台自己跑：加载时、每个凭据事件之后、
以及每半小时一次的定时器，静默发出同一次每日签到——成功按北京日记下，
失败就等下一个事件或下一轮再试。桌面版 OpenCode 在自己的窗口里带着
同一个面板——入口在侧边面板启动器，走包里 `./gui-experimental` 的桌面
GUI 入口；这个名字里的 experimental 是上游的原话：GUI 插件 API 尚属
实验性，可能随桌面版更迭变动。

### magpie 专属的部分

用量卡片、签到开关与生图模型花名册挂在 magpie 自己的宿主扩展钩子上
——这些仍是 magpie 专属，而上面的 `/loomy` 面板把积分数字带到了 v2
TUI 里。v2 侧的插件是手机验证码登录、实时模型清单、网关对话，以及
面板。

## 登录

登录走 Loomy 的手机验证码流程，分两步：

- magpie 先收集手机号（中国大陆 11 位；校验前会清洗掉前缀 `+86`/`86`、
  空格与连字符）；
- 插件发送短信验证码（五分钟有效），magpie 弹出六位验证码输入框，
  插件拿验证码换会话。

会话有效期十四天，Loomy 没有续期接口。会话失效时（HTTP 401/403，或业务码
`020002`/`100002`），插件把登录态标记为过期，magpie 会要求重新短信登录——
没有别的路可走。账号 id 是掩码手机号（`138****8000`）；Loomy 的 userid
随凭据一并保存。

账号主机会对两个登录调用校验 HMAC-SHA1 签名。
签名只属于账号平面——网关平面从不签名。

## 请求

对话是 OpenAI Chat（`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`），发往
`https://loomyad.xunfei.cn/api/v1/chat/completions`，请求体原样透传。
会话 token 放进网关读取的两个头——`token:` 与 `Authorization: Bearer`，
即客户端自己的双写。

积分为零或额度用尽的拒绝（文案带出这层意思的 402、403 或 429）会改写成
429 `rate_limit_error`，magpie 由此把对话切到另一个账号。其余任何
401/403 都是登录态的终点。

## 模型

登录后，模型清单实时读取自 `GET /api/v1/models`：capabilities 变成
工具 / 思考 / 图片位，上下文与输出上限原样透传，reasoning-effort 变体
按厂商文档策展的逐模型表（DeepSeek 与 GLM 为 low/high/max，qwen 为
low/medium/xhigh，MiMo 无挡位，Spark 为 none/low/high），表内没有
的行按该行 `reasoning_efforts` 声明原样透传，只有不声明的行才兜底
low/medium/high 三档。网关把积分倍率拼在展示名尾部
（`MiniMax M3 （x4.0）`——半角全角括号都出现）；插件把后缀拆下来——
名字保持干净，倍率挂到模型记录上，宿主选择器读的正是这个字段。
上游自己声明免费的模型——名字里带「免费」二字，或倍率恰为零——
带 `free` 位；完全没有倍率的不算免费。不是 chat 模型的行不会进聊天
清单：生图模型在 `type` 里就这么声明，而且 id 和名字带着生图模型的
字眼——与宿主自己的图像模型目录同一套词，所以连完全不带 `type` 的行
也照排不误：跟它聊天就是一次失败。

生图模型由插件自己的花名册放回清单旁边——插件为下面三个背书，各自用
花名册给的展示名，线上行自己的事实（上下文与输出上限、能力位）随行，
记录的 `api.url` 指向网关自己的图像路由 `{apiBase}/images/generations`，
不是 chat 那条。
一条目只在实时目录还认它 id 的时候在表里：Loomy 下架某个生图模型，
下一次应答它就消失，不需要发版；Loomy 新增的，则等把它写进花名册的
那一版。兜底表里没有生图条目——没有实时应答就无法证明它还在，
而「失效了还挂着入口」正是花名册要防的事。宿主侧，列进清单的生图
模型在 id 命中宿主自己的图像模型词表时（`qwen-image`、`seedream`……
`Hy-Image` 不在其列）会进提供方的「图像模型」行；在宿主学会把插件的
生图模型挪出聊天清单之前（yetone/magpie#2792），它们也会以 chip 的
形式留在模型列表里：不勾选即可，没有 agent 会跟它们对话。

实时清单是唯一事实来源，一应答即生效。没有会话、应答为空或请求失败时，
插件回落到代码里的内置表——2026-11-17 同一份目录文本模型的快照，
只随网关目录自身的变迁而过期；快照里的倍率与 free 位随表一并发回宿主，
请求失败也会如实标注，让编辑器知道这份清单是插件的默认表、不是账号的。
下表是网关当天实际返回的目录，
留在这里作实地参考：

## 用量

用量卡展示 Loomy 的两个钱包：

- 余额行：永久 + 每日赠送相加（应答自带总额时用它的）；
- 每日赠送窗口：赠送的已消耗份额作为百分比，旁边是限额内还剩多少。
  `dailyBalance` 是赠送的*剩余*（`dailyQuota` − `dailyConsumed`），所以
  百分比需要赠送的额度：应答自带那对字段时用它的，否则用签到按账号记下的
  `dailyQuota`——笔记存在凭据本身上（宿主自己的存储，插件升级也带着；
  宿主没有这种存储时由插件旁的小文件顶上）。卡片在任何地方都找不到笔记时，
  会自己去问 first-login 的应答——只问一次，该调用按天幂等（客户端本来
  每次登录都调它）——所以新装插件在第一次渲染就自愈，不必等下一次签到；
  不发明份额，不假设额度。窗口带着周期的精确重置时刻——签到应答所标注
  那个日的下一个北京零点——卡片因此倒数到真实的续满，而不是猜出来的时刻；
- 永久行摆在旁边：永久余额，没有窗口可消耗；
- 新手行随行：一次性新手任务（共 10000 积分）还有未领时显示——一个
  aside，绝不是百分比：一次花完的钱包没有窗口可消耗。签到领取它们；
  签到跑过之前，这一行说的是还能领多少。

Loomy 没有专门的余额或签到端点：摘要搭在 points-records 调用上，
「签到」就是 Loomy 客户端每次登录都会调的 first-login。服务端每天把
每日赠送续满一次，应答的 `alreadyProcessed` 区分当天的续满与重复：重复
报 *done*（「今日已刷新」，附赠送还剩多少），当天第一次报 *claimed*——
应答带着完整算式（`dailyQuota` − `dailyConsumed`）时把获得量作为 credit，
否则在消息里报剩余。

## 签到

每日自动运行是 magpie 的，不是插件的：**Daily check-in** 开关在
Settings → Usage → Plugins，随 **magpie ≥ v0.1.1083** 提供，**默认关闭**——
打开后 magpie 每天每账号运行一次刷新（只有失败的结果当天会重试）。
**Check in now** 按钮当场运行一次。OpenCode 不调用这个钩子。

同一次运行还会领取一次性新手任务（八个，共 10000 积分）：串行、分值高的
先领、幂等——其中任何一项被拒绝都不碰每日签到自己的结果。新账号的第一次
签到通常一次同时完成赠送续满与新手钱包入账。

## 已知限制

- **会话十四天，没有续期。** 失效后唯一的路是重新短信登录。
- **积分倍率只存在于展示名后缀。** Loomy 不提供结构化倍率字段；插件把
  后缀拆下来，但无法对目录核验任何数额。
- **图片输入因模型家族而异。** 网关线上行对视觉家族都声明了图片输入
  （2026-11-17 实测：DeepSeek 两行、GLM、qwen、MiMo），插件记录以宿主
  读的各种拼写携带该位——扁平、嵌套、以及 magpie 图片徽标读取的
  `capabilities.input` 映射——徽标因此正常显示。传输形态则是另一回事，
  在早前目录的 `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`（已下架）上验证过：它只认网关
  私有的 `<image_base64>…</image_base64>` 标记（标准 `image_url` 会被当
  文本截断），GLM 系相反——只认 `image_url`，喂标记反而坏。按家族改写
  传输形态是计划中的第二迭代；落地之前，宿主自带的附件流程只有 GLM
  家族可靠，当前 DeepSeek 行的传输形态在此网关上未经验证。
- **`reasoning_effort` 在非思考模型上被忽略。** 变体按厂商文档策展的逐模型
  表（DeepSeek 与 GLM 为 low/high/max，qwen 为 low/medium/xhigh，MiMo 无
  挡位，Spark 为 none/low/high）；表内没有的行跟随每行的
  `reasoning_efforts` 声明原样透传，只有不声明的行才兜底 low/medium/high
  三档；上游对不思考的模型丢弃该字段——已知行为。
  哪些模型思考以实时目录声明为准——2026-11-17 当天大多数文本模型都声明了，
  不只 spark 两个。
- **流式工具调用尚未在真实账号上验证。** 桌面网关的 tool_calls 流式
  没有真机运行的记录在案；这是你的 agent 工具循环第一件要验的事。
  如果失败，toolcall 位会在未来的版本里关掉。
- **新手任务由签到领取。** 八个一次性任务（共 10000 积分）在每次签到时
  查询并领取——串行、分值高的先领、幂等：重复应答 `alreadyCompleted`，
  不会重复到账。其中任何一项被拒绝都不碰每日签到自己的结果，还有未领时
  它们的可领总额以 aside 行显示在卡片上。完成与否由上游自行判定；key
  与分值是客户端自己的任务注册表的。

# Changelog

## 0.2.2 — 2026-11-18

### Fixed

- The models hook's records now spell the capability bits flat as well,
  in models.dev's spelling (`attachment`, `reasoning`, `tool_call`,
  `modalities`), beside the `capabilities` nest OpenCode v1 reads. The
  host passes a models hook's records through verbatim, and a picker
  that reads the badge off the top level (zcode's and workbuddy's
  records spell it there) went unserved: the released 0.2.1 carried the
  nested spelling alone, every vision model's mark unshown on it,
  `deepseek-v4-flash-1017` the one a user noticed. The nest and the
  config hook's table are unchanged; the shape test now checks the flat
  keys against the nest instead of treating them as config keys.

- The same records now carry the input/output boolean mapping inside
  `capabilities`, in OpenCode's own info shape: `input: { text, image }`
  and `output: { text }`, image following the row's vision bit. Read
  2026-11-18 at magpie 0.1.4477, the host hands a models hook's records
  through verbatim and its image badge reads the record's
  `capabilities.input.image` boolean mapping alone. A record that
  spelled image input as top-level `attachment` and the `modalities`
  array alone answered `imageSaid` false, and the host fell back to
  looking the model up by id in its own models.dev catalog: that
  catalog knows `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` and not the gateway's
  `deepseek-v4-flash-1017` alias, so the 1017 badge went missing — the
  config table's row was right, the hook's answer overwriting it. An
  explicit `capabilities.input.image` is what overrides that fallback;
  the config table's own records run the host's `modalities()` over the
  arrays and need no such key. The shape test now covers the mapping
  against the 1017 row's live answer.

  proved no better a source: every thinking row on sale carries the same

  requires at runtime (`solid-js`, the gui module with the registries),
  and the rows are DOM built by hand with Solid's own primitives, no JSX
  to compile. The numbers cross one bridge: the RPC the server part
  registers in `v2Setup` (`loomy-auth-quota`, two methods — `status`, the
  records call through `usageOf` off the credential the connection domain
  holds; `checkin`, the same first-login call worded by the same claim
  reader, the grant's size noted behind it the way the renewal notes it) —
  the window calls it through the app's own client (`ctx.client.rpc`),
  never touching the gateway's credential, which only the server side
  holds. The contract travels as a pure JSON-Schema literal, the bundle's
  copy beside the server's, the tests holding the two together; the
  bundle's own words, its Beijing-time formatting and its readout-to-rows
  read are tested in Node (a `.cjs` requires clean), while the render
  itself — DOM in a window — is not. The GUI API is experimental upstream
  (the `-experimental` export name says so) and may change between desktop
  releases.
- On opencode v2 the day's first-login renewal runs by itself: at load,
  behind every credential event and on a half-hour timer, the same
  once-a-day claim magpie's Daily check-in makes — its success marked per
  Beijing calendar day in the host's storage (a namespaced key on the
  flat shared keyspace), anything less than success left unmarked for the
  next event or tick to retry, and nothing ever reported. The timer's
  clearing rides the plugin cleanup's disposers.
- The points card, the daily check-in and the image-generator roster stay
  magpie-only: they ride the host-extension hooks magpie exposes. The
  `/loomy` panel (above) brings the points' numbers to the v2 TUI itself,
  and the desktop panel beside it brings them to the v2 desktop's own
  windows; the rest of the plugin there is the phone-code sign-in, the
  live model list and the gateway chat.
- The image-generator roster rides beside the chat list from a roster the
  plugin keeps: each row only while the live catalog still names its id —
  a retired one leaves with no release, a new one waits for the release
  that vouches for it, and the fallback tables carry none. A model row
  carrying an image generator's name stays off the chat list even when the
  row ships no `type` at all — the same words the host's own image-model
  catalog reads. This work carried its own v0.1.7 tag; it ships here for
  the first time.

## 0.1.5 — 2026-10-28

### Changed

- The usage card speaks the interface language: the window name, the
  unit and the check-in wording follow the `lang` in the host's
  settings.json (zh keeps 每日赠送/永久积分, anything else takes the
  English strings), the unit riding the host dictionary either way.

  failed, points query failed, the hosts' HTTP errors, the account
  fallback).
- The Chinese README moved to `docs/README.zh.md` — npm's readme picker
  reads the package root, where the English `README.md` now stands alone.
- The READMEs tell the protocol's facts and leave the override knobs out
  of the public docs.

### Fixed

- The built-in fallback model table is the catalog observed on 2026-10-28
  (the retired ids are gone; the ten chat entries carry their rates, free
  bits, context and output limits as the gateway served them).
- The quota note's file write is serialized: two accounts signing in at
  once no longer race the read-merge-write and drop each other's note.
- A refused self-heal ask retries after ten minutes instead of never.

## 0.1.4 — 2026-10-28

### Added

- A usage card that finds no quota note anywhere — a fresh install, an
  upgrade that wiped the file, a credential that lost its fields — asks
  the first-login answer itself, once per run: the call is idempotent for
  the day (the client makes it on every login), so the percentage heals
  on the first render instead of waiting for the next check-in. A refusal
  is remembered for the run, never retried on every render.
- The daily window carries `resetsAt` — the next Beijing midnight of the
  cycle date the first-login answer names — so the card counts down to
  the real refill; the consumed share rides as `amount` with
  `limit`/`unit` beside the display (the host renders `limit − amount`
  as what is left), and the display reads `2659 / 5000 积分`.
- A model the upstream itself declares free (the words 免费, or a rate of
  exactly `x0.0`) carries a `free` bit; no rate at all is not free. Rows
  that aren't chat models — the image generators — are left off the list.
- A Chinese README (`README.zh.md`) at the package root, translating the
  English one; the English `README.md` stays the default.

### Fixed

- The noted daily quota no longer dies with the plugin directory: the
  note now lives on the credential itself — the host's own user data,
  carried across plugin upgrades and scoped to the account — with the
  small file beside the plugin kept as the fallback (a host without that
  store) and as the read-behind (an upgrade from a release that noted
  only there). An upgrade-installed plugin no longer needs a fresh
  check-in before the percentage comes back.

## 0.1.3 — 2026-10-28

The first npm release: it carries the work of the three earlier tags
that were never installable — 0.1.0's initial features, 0.1.1's fixes and
0.1.2's rename (published briefly, then unpublished) — with this
version's own work on top.

### Added

- Phone-code sign-in (SMS, a fourteen-day session), the OpenAI-compatible
  model gateway with the live model list, the dual point wallets on the
  usage card, and the daily first-login refresh.
- The newcomer tasks (onboarding): the eight one-off tasks worth 10000
  points in all are claimed by the check-in — serially, highest value
  first, idempotent on the upstream's `alreadyCompleted`; a refusal among
  them never touches the daily claim's own result. The usage card carries
  an aside row with the still-claimable sum while any of it stands (one
  read per session per run; the check-in's round clears it).
- `LOOMY_QUOTA_CACHE_FILE` moves the quota cache file.

### Changed

- The package is published as `@roadkid/opencode-loomy-auth`, renamed
  from `@magpie-community/opencode-loomy-auth` — a scope this plugin has
  not joined, whose name could not be published from this account
  (0.1.2, published briefly, was unpublished and ships with this
  version).
- Docs: the README's model table records the catalog the gateway served on
  2026-10-28, and the docs' wording is tightened throughout.

### Fixed

- The usage card's percentage was forever 0%: the pair it computed from
  (`dailyRemainingPoints`/`dailyLimitPoints`) never comes back from the
  live upstream, and the `dailyBalance` the card fell back to showing
  alone is the grant's *remaining*, not its size. The consumed share now
  reads `(quota − remaining) / quota` off the remaining, with the quota
  taken from the answer when it carries one (`dailyQuota`, or the older
  pair) or from the size the check-in notes per account — kept in memory
  for the run and in a `.loomy-quota.json` beside the plugin across
  restarts, so it takes a check-in (the Daily check-in switch, or Check
  in now) to write the first note. Without a quota the card shows the
  remaining alone; no share is invented and no quota is assumed. (#1)
- The check-in reported *claimed* for every success. The answer's
  `alreadyProcessed` tells the day's renewal from a repeat: a repeat now
  reports *done* (「今日已刷新」, with what is left of the grant), and the
  day's first reports *claimed* — with the gain as its credit when the
  answer carries the whole arithmetic (`dailyQuota` − `dailyConsumed`).
  (#1)
